title: Skills index queries: list rows, per-agent state, native rows, filters
description: Add a at-db query module `skills_index` over `items`, `item_versions`, `native_items`, `deployments` and `sources`. Provide `list_skills(filter)` returning `SkillRow { item_id, name, scope, state, shadowed_by, deployed: BTreeMap<AgentId, DeploymentState>, native_path, update_available, updated_at }`, plus `skill_counts_by_scope`, `skill_counts_by_filter` and `search_skills(query)`. Filters: scope, include_native, shadowed_only, not_in_agentuna, agent, text. All queries parameterized; no filesystem access.
acceptance: `list_skills` over 500 seeded skills returns one row per skill per scope in under 50 ms on the dev Mac (timed test).
Rows carry per-agent deployment state for claude_code, codex, omp, cursor and a native_path for folders present only in agent dirs.
`not_in_agentuna` returns only unadopted native items; `shadowed_only` returns only lower-precedence copies and each row names the winning scope.
`search_skills('rev')` ranks `code-review` before `review-standards` and matches description substrings case-insensitively.
Query unit tests run against the TF-010 fixture DB and touch no real home directory.
notes: May add migration v2 columns/indexes: items(kind,scope,name), deployments(item_id,agent_id), native_items(kind,scope).

title: Skill version history and operation linkage
description: Write one `item_versions` row per successful skill write (sha256 over sorted relative paths plus bytes), linked to the `operations` row and scope. Add queries `versions_for(item_id, scope)` returning newest-first versions with timestamp, operation kind (create, edit, promote, move, import, update, delete), actor and hash, and `version_content(version_id)` for diffing against current.
acceptance: Every successful skill write inserts exactly one item_versions row whose hash changes when any byte of any file in the skill folder changes.
`versions_for` returns newest first and joins operation kind and operation_files count; deleted skills keep their version rows.
`version_content` returns the stored file map so the UI can diff a version against the current SKILL.md.
Migration v2 is additive; existing databases upgrade without data loss and a rebuild-from-files test leaves history intact.
notes: History is not rebuildable from files by design; document that in the DB module.

title: Source and update-tracking metadata
description: Source and update-tracking repository over the TF-015 sources table, per item and scope: kind (git, marketplace, library, folder, zip), url, ref, subpath, commit_sha, content_hash, marketplace_id, install_count, last_checked_at, etag, ignored_sha, local_modified and auto_update (0 off, 1 on, 2 inherit). No DDL here. Queries `source_for`, `update_candidates`, `effective_auto_update(item_id)` resolving the per-item override against the global settings key `auto_update_skills` (owned by TF-023) default off.
acceptance: Importing or linking writes exactly one source row per item and scope; re-import updates it in place.
`update_candidates` returns git and marketplace sources whose remote_sha differs from commit_sha and excludes rows with ignored_sha equal to the remote sha.
`effective_auto_update` returns off when the item is inherit and the global setting is off, and the item override otherwise.
A deleted source row is archived (`deleted_at` set), never hard-deleted, so history can explain origin.
notes: `local_modified` is set when the on-disk hash diverges from content_hash; auto-update uses it to skip.

title: Presets repository and applied-ratio queries
description: Preset repository and queries over the TF-017 tables (presets, preset_members, preset_applications, preset_application_members). No DDL: this story creates no tables and owns no migration. Queries: preset list with member counts, resolved members with current existence, `applied_ratio(preset_id, target)` returning enabled/total plus per-member booleans, and `application_members(application_id)` returning item_id plus prior_enabled for exact unapply. Name uniqueness is enforced by the TF-017 UNIQUE(name, scope) constraint and surfaced as a typed error.
acceptance: Inserting a preset whose name already exists in the same scope returns `DuplicatePresetName`, mapped from the TF-017 UNIQUE(name, scope) constraint.
A preset with 7 existing members and 2 enabled returns ratio `2/7` with member-level booleans; all enabled returns `7/7` and a complete flag.
`preset_application_members` rows record `prior_enabled` for every changed member, and `application_members` returns them in insertion order.
Deleting a skill or server cascades its preset_members rows and the ratio denominator drops to the remaining existing members.
No DDL exists in this story; tests run against the TF-017 schema and a schema snapshot asserts this story adds no tables or columns.
notes: TF-017 currently lists name as globally UNIQUE; the repository expects UNIQUE(name, scope). Flagged to the integrator. preset_application_members is required by CONTRACT decision 8 and decision 7 (undo).

title: Skill model and SKILL.md parser/validator
description: Add `at-model` skill types and a parser in at-engine (module `skills::doc`) using saphyr. Parse leading YAML frontmatter delimited by `---`, require `name` (slug: 1 to 64 chars, lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen) and `description` (trimmed, 1 to 1024 chars). Preserve unknown keys verbatim and the body as raw bytes with byte offsets. Reject missing frontmatter, invalid YAML, missing fields and name/folder mismatch (error for create, warning for import). Never re-serialize the document: edits patch only the target scalar span.
acceptance: A valid file parses into `SkillDoc { name, description, raw, frontmatter_span, body_span, unknown_keys }` with byte offsets that map to the original file.

Each malformed case returns a distinct error variant: missing frontmatter, unclosed `---`, invalid YAML, missing name, uppercase name, space in name, 65-char name, empty description, 1025-char description.
CRLF and UTF-8 BOM files parse; description edits rewrite only the description scalar and leave all other bytes identical.
Parsing a fixture set of 200 real `~/.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` copies yields zero errors.
Name mismatch against the parent folder is a warning for import and a blocking error for create.
notes: Skill spec limits (64/1024) live in constants so they can track Claude Code changes; invalid fixtures are shared with TS-042.

title: Skill templates, slug generation and live preview
description: Implement `SkillTemplate::{Blank, Checklist, Workflow}` rendering a complete SKILL.md (frontmatter, H1, Use when line, template body). `slugify(display_name)` produces the canonical slug; empty results are an error. `render_preview(state)` is a pure function used by the wizard on every keystroke, debounced in the UI.
acceptance: Blank renders minimal frontmatter plus a Usage section; Checklist renders markdown checkboxes; Workflow renders numbered steps plus Inputs and Outputs sections.
`slugify('My Great Skill!')` returns `my-great-skill`; `slugify('Étude')` returns `etude`; `slugify('***')` returns an error.
Preview for a 20 KB description returns in under 5 ms (pure-function benchmark).
All three template outputs parse back through TS-005 with zero errors and correct name/description.
notes: Preview must escape YAML scalars so quotes, colons and newlines in descriptions stay valid.

title: Skill name validation and cross-scope clash detection
description: `check_skill_name(name, target_scope, selected_agents)` validates slug rules and returns `ClashReport { blocking, warnings, hits }`. Checks the item at Global, User, Project and Local, a native folder in each selected agent skills dir, a folder in the target store, case-insensitive collisions on the target filesystem, and reserved names (`agentuna`, `.`, `..`). Each hit carries scope, path and suggested action.
acceptance: Same slug at User while targeting Project returns a non-blocking warning naming the User path; same slug at the target scope returns blocking.
Case-only difference (`Foo` versus `foo`) is blocking on macOS and reports the existing path.
An unmanaged folder `<agent>/skills/<slug>` is blocking with `Adopt` and `Move aside` actions.
Names containing `/`, `..`, spaces, uppercase letters or 65 characters are rejected with a per-rule message.
Checking is read-only: the filesystem is never modified and symlinks are lstat-checked, not followed.
notes: Filesystem path checks reuse at-fs helpers; adapter skills dirs come from TS-025.

title: Canonical skill folder read and write (multi-file packages)
description: Add `at-store` module `skill_package`: read and write `<store>/skills/<slug>/` containing SKILL.md plus auxiliary files (scripts, references, assets). Preserve relative paths and executable bits, reject `..`, absolute paths and escaping symlinks, cap at 200 files and 10 MB per skill, commit atomically via temp directory plus rename, and refuse to overwrite a foreign folder via the TF-005 guard.
acceptance: Round trip of a package with `SKILL.md`, `scripts/x.sh` (mode 0755) and `references/a.md` preserves bytes and permissions.
A path containing `..` or a symlink pointing outside the skill directory returns `InvalidPackage` and writes nothing.
201 files or 11 MB total is rejected with a typed error naming the exceeded limit.
Overwriting an AgenTuna-owned skill backs up first; overwriting a foreign folder fails with the absolute path and no writes.
A crash between temp write and rename leaves no partial folder under skills/ (simulated failure test).
notes: Hash function from TS-002 is computed over the written package; coordinate directory rename semantics with TC central-store layout.

title: Skills index service: merge canonical, native and deployment state
description: `at-engine::skills::index` composes list rows from DB rows and live adapter paths: canonical items, deployments, native items and sources. Item state and sync labels are delegated to the TA-005 derivation; this story owns row composition, per-agent cell state (linked, not linked, native path, none, locked, shadowed), filter counts, sorting and search. Uses TA-001 precedence results instead of reimplementing scope logic.
acceptance: Fixture with 3 canonical, 2 native and 1 shadowed skill returns exactly the expected states and chip counts (All 6, Not in AgenTuna 2, Shadowed 1).
A skill with an enabled deployment plus a newer source commit reports Update available, and Shadowed takes precedence when both apply.
Agent cells name the exact path for native rows and the lock reason for locked rows.
Row assembly does no per-row filesystem walk; adapter paths are fetched once per scope (asserted by call counter).
Source disappearance (deleted agent folder) yields Error state with remediation text instead of a panic.
notes: Consumes the scope precedence resolver owned by the TA slice; no scope logic duplicated here.

title: Enable and disable a skill for one agent
description: Skill-specific enable intent `SetSkillAgentEnabled { item, scope, agent, enabled }`. Planning and deployment mode reuse the TA-008 intent pipeline and TA-015 deployment planner; this story owns the skill package deployment: ensure `<agent skills dir>/<slug>` links (or copies per TA-014 mode) to the store folder, record the deployment, remove only AgenTuna-owned links on disable (copy backed up), and refuse locked items, missing agents (`AgentNotInstalled`) or unmanaged folders (`NativeConflict { path, actions: [Adopt, MoveAside] }`). For Local scope the target is the project agent skills folder and the adapter maintains the `.git/info/exclude` entry (decision 17).
acceptance: Enabling creates a symlink at the adapter path, with Local scope using the project agent skills folder and a `.git/info/exclude` entry, plus a deployments row with mode linked and state In sync; disabling removes only that link and leaves the store folder untouched.
An unmanaged target folder is never modified; the call returns NativeConflict with the absolute path and both actions.
A missing agent returns AgentNotInstalled and writes nothing; a locked item returns Locked and produces no ChangeSet.
Copy-mode agents receive a recursive copy and disabling it creates a backup catalogue entry before removal.
Enable is idempotent: applying the same state twice produces no second operation row.
notes: One intent per agent toggle so the UI can report per-agent results; bulk version is TS-015.

title: Disable a skill in this repo (local override)
description: `DisableSkillInRepo { skill_slug, agents }` writes a skill-specific tombstone entry into the project store `store.json` `disabled` array as `{ item_id, kind, agents }` (schema and atomic writer owned by TC-002, decision 16), removes Project/Local deployments for the selected agents, and marks the item Disabled here. Resolution semantics for the tombstone come from TA-003; this story owns the skill entry writer, deployment cleanup and idempotency. Re-enable removes only that entry.
acceptance: After disabling an inherited skill, the effective list excludes it and detail shows Disabled here with the source scope and agent list.
A locked Global item cannot be disabled: returns Locked with an explanatory message and writes nothing.
The `disabled` entry is written through TC-002's store.json writer atomically and backed up; a second disable call is a successful no-op with no new operation.
Re-enable restores the exact deployment set that existed before the disable (tree hash comparison).
notes: TC-002 owns the store.json `disabled` array schema; TA-003 owns tombstone resolution; this story writes the skill entry and cleans deployments. UI is TS-037.

title: Skill shadow detection and compare-copies payload
description: Consume the shadow ordering produced by the TA-001 scope resolver and add the skill-specific compare payload: `CompareCopies { a, b }` with scope, absolute path, full SKILL.md text, folder hash, mtime and deployment list for each side. Local disable removes a copy from the effective set but keeps it available for comparison. Locks do not create shadowing. The UI uses this payload for the compare dialog and shadow note.
acceptance: Same slug at User and Project yields Project as winner, User shadowed, and the detail note names Project as the winning scope.
Three scopes produce two shadowed copies and an ordered compare chain from nearest to farthest.
Compare reads both SKILL.md files and hashes both folders; an externally edited copy with a newer mtime still compares cleanly.
Identical hashes return `identical: true` and the UI can disable Keep actions.
A missing file on one side returns a typed `CopyUnreadable` error with path instead of failing the whole list.
notes: Uses the scope ordering from the TA resolver; shadowing semantics are tested in TS-043.

title: Promote, move and duplicate a skill between scopes
description: Intents: Promote (copy to a broader scope and keep the source), Move (copy, re-point deployments, back up and delete the source) and Duplicate (copy within the same scope under a new slug). Preflight clash detection; when the target copy exists return `OverwritePrompt { target_path, target_hash, source_hash }` requiring explicit Replace (backup target first) or Rename. The whole action is one ChangeSet with history rows.
acceptance: Promote Project to User writes the User copy, keeps Project, updates deployments and marks the Project copy shadowed.
Move leaves no gap: after apply, every enabled agent resolves to the new location and the old folder exists only in backups.
Promote without confirmation over an existing target is refused; with Replace the target backup is restorable and the operation log names both paths.
Duplicate `review` to `review-2` succeeds, and duplicate to an existing slug returns the clash report.
Promote to Global without the admin permission flag returns PermissionDenied and writes nothing.
notes: Backup catalogue and restore come from TF-004; overwrite dialog UI is TS-037.

title: Delete a skill from a scope with backup
description: `DeleteSkill { item, scope }` requires `confirmed=true`. Backs up the full skill folder, removes AgenTuna-owned deployments, deletes the canonical folder and item row while retaining version history, and archives the sources row. Returns `next_effective` when a lower-precedence copy exists so the UI can explain what loads instead. Undo is the generic TC-010 `undo_operation(operation_id)`, not a skill-local restore path. Never deletes unmanaged or native folders.
acceptance: Calling without `confirmed=true` returns ConfirmationRequired and performs no writes.
After delete, the backup directory holds the complete skill package and a backups row, and TC-010 `undo_operation` restores it byte-identically within the 30-day window.
Deleting the User copy while a Project copy exists makes the Project copy effective and unshadowed, reported in `next_effective`.
Attempting to delete a native or unmanaged folder returns RefusedUnmanaged with the path.
Deployment symlinks are removed without following them; copies are backed up before removal.
notes: Undo entry reuses TF-009 operation log; confirmation UI is TS-037.

title: Bulk skill operations as a single ChangeSet
description: `BulkIntent { kind: Promote | Enable | Move | Disable, items, targets }` preflights every item, builds one ChangeSet and applies it atomically. Preflight failures abort before any write and return per-item reasons. A post-apply failure triggers rollback of already-applied operations. Emits progress events (item started, done, failed) for the UI.
acceptance: Five selected items with one locked item produce zero filesystem writes and a per-item reason list.
Bulk enabling 3 skills for 2 agents creates 6 links, one operations row and 6 operation_files rows.
An injected permission failure on the second link rolls back the first and restores deployments to the pre-state tree hash.
Progress events arrive for every item and the UI receives one Tauri progress event per batch.
Bulk operations with zero valid items return `NothingToDo` and write nothing.
notes: All-or-nothing is the contract; partial success is not offered. UI bulk bar is TS-029.

title: Add-skill wizard state machine
description: `ui/src/screens/add_skill::state::AddSkillWizard` with steps Source, Details, ScopeAgents, Review, Done. `SourceKind::{New, Git, Library, Marketplace, Folder, Zip}` selects the Details panel. Per-step validation gates Next; Back preserves all entered state; Cancel discards a clean draft silently and asks for confirmation when dirty. Fetch or clone runs only through explicit events. No filesystem or network calls inside the state machine; providers are injected so the UI owns navigation and gating while engine stories own the work.
acceptance: Forward navigation Source to Details to ScopeAgents to Review to Done works only when each step validates; jumps beyond an invalid step are rejected.
Back from Review to Details then forward again retains name, template, fetched repo selection and chosen agents.
Cancel on a dirty wizard returns `DiscardDraft`; on a clean wizard it discards immediately; neither writes files.
Each SourceKind selects its matching Details panel and its required fields are validated (repo URL, library selection, marketplace id, folder path, zip path).
A unit test drives every transition with mock providers and asserts zero filesystem or network access.
notes: State struct is serializable for tests and for crash-safe draft persistence later. UI is TS-031 to TS-036.

title: Add-skill review plan and optional git stage
description: Build the exact `FilePlan` for a wizard result: canonical files to create with absolute paths, deployments per agent with link or copy target, overwrite entries with diffs against existing files, and an optional `git add` list. The stage option appears only for Project scope inside a git repository. Staging runs after a successful write and only stages the created paths; it never commits.
acceptance: The plan lists every path that will be created plus every link target, and no path lies outside the store or a configured agent directory.
The stage option is hidden for Global and User scopes and for projects that are not git repositories.
`git add` runs only after a successful apply, stages exactly the created paths and creates no commit.
An existing-file collision shows an overwrite entry with a unified diff instead of being silently skipped.
Applying the plan produces a filesystem tree identical to the plan listing (test compares sets).
notes: Git stage calls at-git; dry-run mode returns the plan without applying for the Review step.

title: Library import from other scopes and projects with Copy or Link
description: Enumerate importable skills from every other scope store and every registered project store into `LibrarySource { label, path, kind, count }` plus skill rows with parse state. Copy materializes an independent package in the target store. Link creates a symlink at the target store skills path to the source folder and records source kind library with link mode. Sources are read-only and never modified.
acceptance: The source list contains one entry per other scope with a count plus one per registered project with a count; empty sources are omitted.
Copy produces an independent folder: editing the target does not change the source and hashes diverge.
Link stores mode link, reads through to the source folder, and a deleted source surfaces BrokenLink state with the missing target path.
A name clash in the target blocks that skill with a reason while other selected skills still import.
Importing from a read-only source directory succeeds with copy and fails with link with a typed PermissionDenied error.
notes: Project registry comes from at-db projects table; UI is TS-034.

title: Folder and zip skill import with zip-slip protection
description: `import_folder(path)` detects a single skill (SKILL.md at root) or multiple skills (children containing SKILL.md) and returns candidates with parsed name and description. `import_zip(path)` validates the archive before extraction: reject absolute entry names, `..` components, symlink or device entries, encrypted entries, more than 2000 entries and more than 25 MB uncompressed. Extract only into a temp dir under the AgenTuna cache, then reuse folder import, and remove the temp dir on success, failure and cancel.
acceptance: A zip containing `../evil/SKILL.md` is rejected with ZipSlip naming the entry before any extraction outside the temp dir; the store tree is unchanged.
A zip with 2001 entries or 26 MB uncompressed is rejected with a limit message naming the exceeded bound.
A folder with nested skills lists candidates with parsed name, description and validity; invalid children are shown with their parse error instead of hidden.
Temp directories are removed on success, error and cancel (asserted by a test hook listing the cache dir).
A zip whose single root folder wraps the skills is unwrapped, and a zip with two root skills returns both as candidates.
notes: Archive reading uses the zip crate with streaming entry checks; symlink-aware checks are covered in TS-045.

title: Git skill import: clone, discover, preview and pick
description: at-git `clone_for_import(url, ref)` clones depth 1 into a temp directory with a timeout and no credential prompts. Discover `SKILL.md` up to depth 6, skipping `.git`, `node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`, `.next` and `vendor`, capped at 500 candidates. Parse each with TS-005 and return `GitSkillCandidate { subpath, name, description, valid, error }` plus the resolved commit sha. Import selected candidates through TS-008 and record the source row. Clean up the temp clone on finish, error and cancel.
acceptance: A file:// fixture repo with 3 skills returns 3 candidates with correct subpaths and the commit sha.
A failed clone returns CloneFailed with the stderr tail and leaves no temp directory behind.
A private repository without credentials returns AuthRequired; no credential prompt or keychain access happens in this path.
Selecting 2 of 3 candidates imports only those two and each source row records url, commit sha and subpath.
A repository with more than 500 SKILL.md files returns the first 500 with a truncation warning flag.
notes: URL schemes allowed: https, ssh git@, file (tests only). Depth and cap constants shared with TS-045.

title: Marketplace client for skills.sh
description: Add `at-git::marketplace`: explicit search and refresh over the skills.sh HTTP API returning `MarketplaceSkill { id, name, description, author, installs, source_url, updated_at }`. Every call is registered as NetworkAction::MarketplaceBrowse or MarketplaceInstall under TF-036 and is denied before DNS unless the policy permits it. Responses cached on disk under the AgenTuna cache with a 1 hour TTL and ETag; no request at startup or when the Skills screen opens. Offline or DNS failure returns cached rows with `offline=true`. Install resolves `source_url` and hands off to TS-020, recording kind marketplace and the install count snapshot.
acceptance: A startup test asserts zero marketplace network calls until the user triggers Search, Refresh or opens the marketplace source.
Search results include install counts and source URLs; a 200-entry cached page serves in under 100 ms.
Offline returns the cached result set with `offline=true` and does not raise an error dialog or toast loop.
Cache entries are keyed by normalized query, expire after 1 hour, and are served with a stale warning when offline.
An installed marketplace skill writes a source row with kind marketplace, marketplace_id, install_count and the resolved git commit.
notes: TF-036 owns the allow-list; this story never calls HTTP outside a registered NetworkAction. Endpoint shape must be re-verified against skills.sh during implementation.

title: Presets: create, apply, unapply and applied ratio
description: `PresetService` over TS-004: create, rename, delete presets and add or remove skill and MCP server members. `apply(preset, Target::Agent(agent))` enables missing member skills for that agent and loads member servers; `apply(preset, Target::Repo(project))` enables members into the Project scope. One ChangeSet per apply, writing one `preset_application_members` row per changed member with its `prior_enabled` value. `unapply` restores exactly those prior values. Returns the applied ratio before and after.
acceptance: Creating a preset with 3 skills and 1 server persists it with member count 4 and returns it in the list.
Applying to an agent enables only missing members, moves the ratio from `2/4` to `4/4`, and a second apply is a no-op with no operation row.
Unapply restores each changed member to the `prior_enabled` value recorded in `preset_application_members`, so members enabled before the preset stay enabled.
A locked or deleted member blocks the whole apply with a per-member reason and writes nothing.
A deleted member is excluded from the ratio denominator with a warning state until the member row is pruned.
notes: TF-017 owns the tables (including preset_application_members). MCP member enablement is delegated to TM-004; this story owns the preset transaction and ordering.

title: Source tracking and update check for git skills
description: Record source metadata at import and check for updates: resolve the remote default branch sha via `git ls-remote` (no fetch into the store), compare with the stored commit, compute whether local content diverged from the imported hash, and set `update_available` with `remote_sha`, `local_modified` and `checked_at`. Checks run only on an explicit Check for updates action unless auto-update is enabled. Handle offline, deleted branch and force-push as typed results that never produce a false badge.
acceptance: A fixture remote advanced by one commit yields update_available true with remote_sha differing from commit_sha and a badge state.
An unchanged remote yields false and only updates last_checked_at.
Offline returns Unknown, preserves the previous state and does not change the badge.
A deleted remote branch returns SourceGone and a warning state, not an update badge.
No network call occurs when auto-update is off and the user has not asked for a check (test asserts zero git invocations).
notes: `git ls-remote` is used to avoid writing into the store; at-git wraps it with timeout and typed errors.

title: Auto-update policy and apply
description: Global settings key `auto_update_skills` (TF-023, default off) plus per-skill tri-state (on, off, inherit). When effective policy is on, skills are checked at launch and on a configurable interval, and clean skills are updated: diff remote against local, skip when local_modified, otherwise back up, write the new package, bump commit_sha, redeploy no-op and record an operation. Never runs while the wizard is open or a SKILL.md editor has unsaved changes.
acceptance: Default off: a launch test with auto-update disabled performs zero network calls.
An enabled clean skill updates, history records operation kind update, and the badge clears.
A skill edited locally after import is skipped with local_modified set; its badge stays and an explicit override updates it with a backup and diff preview.
A failed update keeps the previous files byte-identical, records a failure operation and remains retryable.
Auto-update is paused while an editor has unsaved changes and resumes on save or discard.
notes: Auto-update is opt-in, so scheduled network use complies with X09. The global key lives in TF-023; the per-skill override is in sources.auto_update. UI settings are TS-040.

title: Skill folder deployment capability per agent adapter
description: Add skill deployment methods to the agent adapters delivered by the TA slice, without redefining their path tables: `deploy_skill` and `undeploy_skill` on `AgentAdapter`, first-enable creation of the skills directory, and mode wiring from TA-014 (link, copy, junction fallback). For Local scope the adapter returns the project agent skills folder (for example `.claude/skills`), and each deployed Local path is added to `.git/info/exclude` so it is never committed (decision 17). Path discovery, install detection and version probing stay in TA-021, TA-023, TA-025, TA-027 and TA-032. On this Mac omp uses managed-skills and falls back to skills.
acceptance: Each adapter returns the documented path; omp prefers managed-skills and falls back to skills when the former does not exist (temp HOME tests).
A not-installed agent reports NotInstalled; no directory is created anywhere for it.

Link versus copy honors the per-agent setting, the copy fallback produces a complete recursive copy, and a Local-scope deploy adds its exact path to `.git/info/exclude` exactly once (idempotent on re-deploy).
Deploying an identical existing AgenTuna-owned link is a no-op; deploying over a foreign folder returns the unmanaged conflict.
Windows-only junction fallback compiles behind cfg and is covered by a unit test of the strategy ordering.
notes: Adapter trait and per-agent path tables are owned by the TA slice (TA-020 to TA-032); this story adds the skill deployment capability and must not duplicate path detection. Research correction: omp real path is managed-skills, so both are detected.

title: Native skill discovery in agent folders
description: Adapter-level `list_native_skills` capability consumed by TC-006. For each installed agent skills dir, return `NativeSkill { path, name, description, valid, error, agent, scope, mtime, target }` for folders not owned by AgenTuna. Links whose target resolves into the AgenTuna store are classified Managed and excluded from native rows (decision 12). Dangling symlinks report Broken with target. Malformed SKILL.md rows are listed with a parse error, not dropped. Read-only, no adoption logic.
acceptance: A temp HOME with 2 canonical links and 1 unmanaged folder returns exactly 1 native row with its absolute path.
A symlink into the store is excluded; a dangling symlink appears as Broken with target text.
An unparseable SKILL.md still appears with `valid=false` and the parse error reason.
An unreadable folder (mode 000) yields a PermissionDenied row and does not abort the scan of other agents.
Scanning the same tree twice returns identical rows in stable order.
notes: TS-026 is a dependency of TC-006 and must not depend back on it. TC-006 orchestrates the scan; this story supplies per-adapter enumeration and Managed classification. Adoption stays in TC-011.

title: Link strategy and permission handling for skill deployment
description: Skill-specific policy layer on top of the TF-006 symlink/copy primitive: per-agent copy-versus-link choice, creation of relative symlinks on macOS and Linux, Windows policy selection between symlink and junction, cross-volume detection, and normalization of EPERM, EACCES, ENOSPC and EDQUOT into typed `FsError` values with remediation text. Does not reimplement the primitive: all link, junction, copy and lstat-before-replace mechanics come from TF-006.
acceptance: macOS creates `<agent>/<slug>` as a relative symlink resolving to the store folder; reading through it returns SKILL.md bytes.
An existing AgenTuna-owned link is replaced atomically; a foreign link or real folder is refused with its target path.
A parent directory with mode 500 returns PermissionDenied naming the path, with no partial files left.
Windows adjacency code compiles under cfg(windows) and a strategy-ordering unit test asserts symlink then junction then copy.
A cross-volume link attempt returns CrossVolume and, when copy fallback is enabled, falls back to a copy with a warning.
notes: This story adds policy and error translation only; TF-006 owns the primitive mechanics and TC-032 consumes both for migration, so there is no second junction or copy fallback. If TF-006 lacks a needed capability, extend it there rather than forking a skill-local copy.

title: Skills list screen
description: `ui/src/screens/skills`: top bar with scope switcher hook, filter chips (All, Global, User, Project, Not in AgenTuna, Shadowed) with counts, debounced search, virtualized table via TU-003 with name, scope badge, per-agent cells, status and update badge, row menu (Open, Promote, Move to scope, Duplicate, Delete), Adopt and Resolve buttons on native and conflict rows, and a mount point for TC-025's Not in AgenTuna banner. Banner rendering and Hide persistence belong to TC-025, which stores the Hide state in settings `native_banner_hidden.skill`; this screen only mounts it and routes Review and migrate. States: empty with Add skill CTA, loading skeleton, error with retry, populated, shadowed rows dimmed with winner tooltip, following the TU-021 state pattern.
acceptance: A 500-row fixture scrolls at 60 fps and builds fewer than 50 cell widgets per frame (virtualization assertion).
Each chip filters as labelled; Shadowed shows only dimmed rows whose tooltip names the winning scope and path.
Toggling an agent cell calls TS-010; on NativeConflict the toggle reverts and a toast offers Adopt or Move aside, with no optimistic state kept.

Native rows show the adapter path chip and Adopt or Resolve actions; the banner mount renders TC-025's component unchanged and Hide persistence is owned by TC-025 via `native_banner_hidden.skill`, not by this screen.
The empty state CTA opens the add-skill wizard; the error state retries the query and shows the typed error message.
notes: Update badge rendering defined in TS-040; selection column and bulk bar in TS-029. TC banner component is injected via a slot so this screen does not depend on migration internals.

title: Skills multi-select and bulk action bar
description: `ui/src/screens/skills` selection module: checkbox column keyed by item and scope, select all filtered rows, and a bulk bar with Promote, Enable for agent, Move to scope, Disable and Clear. The bar shows the selected count and a hidden-by-filter count. Actions open the relevant dialog once and run TS-015, streaming progress and finishing with a per-item result summary. Selection survives scrolling and filter changes until cleared.
acceptance: Select all selects only currently filtered rows while the count badge reports total selected including rows hidden by a later filter.
Bulk promote opens the scope dialog once, runs a single bulk operation and shows either a success toast with the count or a scrollable failure list.
During a run the bar shows progress and disables actions; Esc and Clear reset the selection.
A preflight failure leaves the table unchanged and lists each blocked row with its reason.
Bulk Enable for agent opens the enable popover once and applies the same agent set to all selected skills.
notes: Result summary uses the toast service for success and an inline expandable panel for failures.

title: Skill detail screen
description: `ui/src/screens/skill_detail`: header with name, scope badge, update badge, absolute path and Open in Finder; rendered SKILL.md via react-markdown with a sanitizer with an Edit action using the TU-008 editor and diff preview; metadata block (description, source, hash, updated, link or copy); enabled-for toggles per agent; shadow note with Compare copies and Keep this copy only; history timeline from TS-002 with diff against current; actions Promote, Delete and Disable in this repo. States: loading, error, not found after external deletion, populated, shadowed.
acceptance: Populated state renders markdown, description, per-agent toggles matching the DB and history newest first with operation kind and time.
A shadowed skill shows the winner scope and both actions; Compare opens the TS-038 dialog prefilled with both copies.
Edit saves through TS-008 with a diff preview and backup, then appends a history entry and shows a success toast.
Not-found state after deletion elsewhere offers Back to Skills and a refresh, without a panic or blank screen.
Watcher refresh preserves scroll position and the selected tab; unsaved editor content blocks the refresh with a prompt.
notes: Open in Finder uses reveal-in-file-manager; no edit path outside the store for native skills, which instead offer Adopt.

title: Add-skill wizard shell, navigation and Done screen
description: `ui/src/screens/add_skill` shell: step indicator for 4 steps plus Done, Back and Next buttons, per-step validation messages, Cancel with discard confirmation, and a content slot per step. Source step shows six cards: Write new, Import from git, From library, Marketplace, Local folder, Zip file. Done shows written files from TS-017, stage-in-git result, Back to Skills, Add another and Edit SKILL.md. Wires TS-016 without embedding business logic in the widget tree.
acceptance: Step indicator reflects current step; Next is disabled while the step is invalid and Back restores previous entries.
Cancel on a dirty wizard asks Discard draft and closes with no files written on confirm; clean cancel closes silently.
Done lists every written path and link target from the plan and the git stage outcome, and Add another resets to Source.
Source cards render disabled reasons when unavailable (for example marketplace blocked by policy) while the rest stay usable.
Esc triggers the cancel path and Enter advances only when valid (O14).
notes: The wizard is a full screen, not a modal, matching the FigCraft flow; dialogs inside it use TU-004.

title: Wizard new-skill step: form, template cards and live preview
description: `ui/src/screens/add_skill::new_skill`: display name field with auto-slug, use-when description with a 1024 counter, template radio cards Blank, Checklist and Workflow, and a split live preview of the generated SKILL.md debounced at 120 ms. Inline validation from TS-005 and TS-007; a clash banner lists other scopes when the name already exists elsewhere and blocks when it exists at the target scope.
acceptance: Typing a name updates the slug and preview; the counter turns red at 1024 and Next is blocked.
Switching template regenerates the preview while preserving name and description.
A name present at another scope shows a warning listing scope and path; presence at the target scope blocks Next.
Preview is read-only, an empty name shows a placeholder and an empty preview with guidance.
Validation messages map one-to-one to parser error variants (no generic invalid message).
notes: Preview uses the same renderer as TS-006 so UI and stored output cannot drift.

title: Wizard git import step
description: `ui/src/screens/add_skill::git_import`: repo URL field, optional ref, Fetch button that is the only network trigger, spinner with Cancel, candidate list with checkboxes, parsed name and description, validity badge and error tooltip, and a SKILL.md preview pane loaded from the temp clone. Select all and none actions. Error states: auth required, clone failed with stderr tail, no skills found.
acceptance: Fetch shows progress and populates the candidate list; an empty result shows No skills found with a hint, no error toast.
Invalid candidates are disabled with their parse error as tooltip and are excluded from select all.
Clicking a candidate renders its SKILL.md from the temp clone without further network calls.
Auth required explains the cause and offers a public URL hint; no credential prompt appears.
Back then forward preserves the fetched list, selection and scroll position.
notes: Cancel during clone cancels the job and deletes the temp directory (bridge handles cleanup).

title: Wizard library import step
description: `ui/src/screens/add_skill::library_import`: source list of other scopes and registered projects with counts and last used, skill list with checkboxes and per-item clash state, a Copy versus Link segmented control with a one-line explanation of each, and a target scope summary. Empty state appears when no other sources exist.
acceptance: Sources render with counts; choosing a project lists that project's skills with paths and clash indicators.
Clashing rows are disabled with a reason and Select all available skips them.
The Copy or Link choice is reflected in the Review plan as a copied folder versus a link path.
No available sources shows an empty state with a shortcut to the git import source.
Switching source keeps already selected skills from other sources visible in a selected summary.
notes: Uses the shared source-list component also used by presets member picker.

title: Wizard marketplace and folder or zip sources
description: `ui/src/screens/add_skill::marketplace` and `::folder_zip`. Marketplace: search field, explicit Search and Refresh, results table (name, author, installs, source) with formatted counts, a data provenance line (skills.sh, cached time), offline banner with cached rows and Retry, and an install action. Folder and zip: native file dialog, path display, detected skill list with checkboxes and preview, and blocking validation errors (zip slip, too large, no SKILL.md) with the offending entry named.
acceptance: Opening the marketplace with no network shows the cached or offline banner instead of an error dialog; no request fires until Search or Refresh.
Results show install counts formatted (for example 1.2k) and selecting one adds it to the wizard selection.
A zip containing a traversal entry shows a blocking error naming the entry and nothing is imported.
A folder containing multiple skills lists candidates with checkboxes and preview; a folder without any SKILL.md shows a clear error.
Progress is visible during download and extraction, and Cancel aborts without leaving temp files.
notes: File dialogs use rfd (native) to stay consistent with macOS; provenance label satisfies the no silent network rule.

title: Wizard scope and agents step plus review step
description: `ui/src/screens/add_skill::scope_agents` and `::review`. Step 3: scope radio cards Global, User, Project plus a collapsed Local (only you, this repo) option that expands to the full card, with lock and admin notes; agent checkboxes with resolved target paths; not-installed agents disabled with Set path opening overlay O11; inline clash results from TS-007. Step 4: summary card including the selected Local scope when chosen, grouped file list (canonical files, deployments) with absolute paths, per-file diff preview for overwrites, stage-in-git checkbox only in a git repository, and the Create action with progress.
acceptance: Changing scope re-runs the clash check and updates every agent target path; expanding Local shows the `.agentuna/local/` store path and the agent-local render targets.
A not-installed agent checkbox is disabled with the reason and Set path opens the connect-agent overlay without losing wizard state.
Review lists exactly the paths returned by TS-017 and shows a diff preview for each overwrite entry.
When Local is selected, Review shows Local in the summary and lists the local store files plus agent-local render targets.
Create streams progress and navigates to Done only after all writes succeed; on failure the wizard stays on Review with the error.
notes: Global scope shows an admin/permission warning before enabling selection, per scope model X01.

title: Promote or move, delete and disable-in-repo dialogs
description: `ui/src/overlays/dialogs`: Promote or Move dialog with target scope cards and paths, overwrite warning containing hash comparison and a diff summary, Replace or Rename choice, backup note, and optional new name; Delete dialog with file list, backup statement, lower-scope copy note and a typed-name confirmation; Disable in this repo dialog explaining the local override, listing affected agents and naming the override file path.
acceptance: Promoting onto an existing copy shows a blocking warning with Replace and Rename; choosing Replace states where the backup will be kept.
Move states the source folder is removed after backup; confirming runs TS-013 and shows a toast with the backup location.
Delete requires typing the skill name; Cancel changes nothing and a successful delete toast offers Undo.
The disable-in-repo dialog names the override file path and the agent links it will remove.
All three dialogs restore focus to the triggering row after close and are dismissible with Esc without acting.
notes: Dialogs never call engine directly; they emit intents handled by the screen controller.

title: Enable-for-agent popover and compare-copies dialog
description: `ui/src/overlays` enable popover anchored to a row or detail cell: installed agent checkboxes with current state, disabled rows with reason, Apply running TS-010 only for changed agents and reporting per-agent results. Compare dialog with a side-by-side diff via TU-007, headers with scope, path, hash and mtime, Keep Project or Keep User actions that copy the chosen version over the other with a backup, and a read-only identical state.
acceptance: Popover reflects current per-agent state and Apply sends only differing agents; results appear per agent or as one combined toast.
A NativeConflict keeps the popover open with Adopt and Move aside actions and leaves the toggle unchanged.
Compare highlights differing lines and shows both paths and hashes; Keep actions create one operation with a backup of the overwritten copy.
Identical copies show No differences with Keep actions disabled.
Popover and dialog are keyboard reachable and close on Esc (O14).
notes: Compare keeps read-only when one copy is native and unmanaged, offering Adopt only.

title: Presets list, editor and apply controls
description: Presets tab inside `ui/src/screens/skills` (or a dedicated screen registered in the sidebar if the integrator prefers): list with name, member count, per-agent applied ratio chips (`2/7`, `4/4`, check), created date; editor to create, rename, delete and toggle member skills and servers; apply menu for an agent or the current project; unapply action. States: empty, loading, error, populated.
acceptance: Empty state offers New preset; the list shows ratios computed from the DB and updates after applies.
Editor add and remove persist immediately and a duplicate preset name is blocked inline.
Apply to agent shows progress then a check chip; unapply restores only the members the application changed.
Deleted or missing members show a warning icon and are excluded from the ratio with explanatory text.
Applying an empty preset is disabled with a tooltip explaining why.
notes: If the shell team prefers a first-class screen, register `presets` in ui/src/shell; the module can live at ui/src/screens/skills::presets either way.

title: Update badge and auto-update settings
description: Update badge on Skills list rows and skill detail with tooltip showing old and new sha, source and last checked; actions Update now, View changes (diff), Ignore this version; a Check for updates action in the list header. Settings section for the global auto-update toggle plus per-skill tri-state on the detail screen; an unknown or offline state renders a muted dot instead of a badge.
acceptance: The badge appears only for sources with update_available; the tooltip lists both shas and the last checked time.
Update now shows a diff preview then applies with a backup, shows a toast and clears the badge.
Ignore stores the ignored sha and hides the badge until a newer remote sha appears.
Global auto-update is off by default and the per-skill tri-state persists across restarts.
Offline or SourceGone renders a muted warning dot with explanatory tooltip, never an update badge.
notes: Reuses the diff viewer from TU-007 and the settings screen from the TU slice.

title: `agentuna skills` CLI command group
description: Owns the `skills` noun group on the shared CLI command tree from TU-026, using the JSON envelope and exit-code contract from TU-033. Commands: `skills list --scope`, `skills show`, `skills install <git-url|marketplace-id|path>` (dispatches to git import, marketplace install or folder import), `skills deploy <name> --agent` (alias of enable), `skills enable/disable --agent`, `skills add --from <path|git-url|marketplace-id>`, `skills remove --yes` with backup, and `skills preset list|apply` (replaces the old `deploy --preset`). No prompts, no TTY requirement, same engine calls as the UI.
acceptance: `skills list --json --scope project` returns a schema-stable object with the skill array, scope and state; a snapshot test guards the schema.

`skills install <path|git-url|marketplace-id>` dispatches to folder, git or marketplace import respectively, and `skills deploy <name> --agent` returns the same JSON result as `skills enable` (alias asserted).
`remove` without `--yes` exits 2 and writes nothing; with `--yes` creates a backup and reports its path.
Commands run without a TTY, emit no ANSI colour under `--json`, and never open a dialog or prompt.
`preset apply` reports the before and after ratio and mirrors the UI ordering of operations.
notes: TU-026 owns the command tree and TU-033 the JSON envelope and exit codes; this story owns the skills noun group, its schemas, skill-specific validation and the install/deploy/remove/preset safeguards. Features left empty intentionally: E12 is the CLI product epic and is covered by TU stories.

title: Golden-file tests for SKILL.md parsing, editing and templates
description: Fixture suite under `at-engine/tests/golden/skills` with curated SKILL.md files: quoted description, multiline folded description, license and metadata blocks, argument-hint, CRLF, BOM, missing name, name mismatch, invalid YAML, 65-char name, 1025-char description, plus golden outputs for all three templates. Tests assert parsed snapshots, byte-stable edits and error variants.
acceptance: At least 20 fixtures, each with a checked-in JSON snapshot of the parse result; every snapshot matches.
Editing the description rewrites only that scalar and the rest of the file is byte-identical (asserted with an explicit unified diff).
Unknown frontmatter keys and key order are preserved exactly.
All three template renders match golden files and re-parse without errors.
Every parser error variant is exercised by at least one fixture.
notes: Fixtures are sanitized copies of real skills; never store secrets or user paths.

title: Shadow and scope precedence matrix
description: Extends the TA-090 scope resolution matrix harness with skill-specific rows: duplicates across Global, User, Project and Local, locks, disable-here, native copies and broken links. Each row asserts winner, shadowed set, effective deployment set, list state, compare chain and explanatory reason. Reuses the TA-090 row builder and TF-010 temp HOME fixtures rather than building a second harness.
acceptance: At least 32 rows cover all four scopes pairwise plus lock and disable-here variations, and all pass.
A locked Global copy cannot be shadowed or disabled and the reason names the lock.
Disable-here removes the item from effective output while keeping it available for comparison.
An unmanaged native copy never silently wins: the row reports Conflict with the path.
List state and detail reason strings are asserted, not just booleans.
notes: Overlaps TA-090 by design only in fixture reuse; TA-090 covers resolution semantics, this story covers skill list and compare presentation.

title: Bulk, promote, move and delete safety tests
description: Integration tests with a temp HOME: bulk enable 5 skills for 2 agents, injected mid-apply failure, promote onto an existing copy with and without confirmation, move, duplicate, and delete with a lower-precedence copy. Assert tree hashes, backups, operation_files, rollback and absence of orphan links.
acceptance: A failure injected on the second of five writes leaves the tree hash identical to the pre-state and returns per-item outcomes.
Every overwritten or deleted file has a backups row and restores byte-identically.
Promote, move and delete never remove or modify an unmanaged folder (asserted by mode and mtime).
After promote and after delete the deployments table matches the filesystem links exactly (no orphans either way).
Each operation appears once in operations history with the correct operation_files count.
notes: Failure injection uses a at-fs test hook that fails a named path, not a mock of the engine.

title: Import security and offline behaviour tests
description: Tests for zip-slip, symlink entries escaping the archive, decompression bombs, oversized archives, folder permission denied, git repos with duplicate skill names across subdirectories, the 500 candidate cap, and marketplace offline and stale-cache paths. Each test asserts the store tree is unchanged on rejection and no temp directories remain.
acceptance: Zips with `..`, absolute paths or symlink entries are rejected before extraction and the store tree hash is unchanged.
A 26 MB or 2001-entry archive is rejected with the limit name; no partial extraction directory remains.
Duplicate skill names in one repository are disambiguated by subpath and never silently overwrite each other.
Offline marketplace returns cached rows with offline=true and no panic or retry storm (request count asserted).
Permission denied on a source folder returns a typed error and cleans up temp directories.
notes: Fixture archives are generated in the test, not committed, to keep the repo small.

title: Presets and update-tracking behaviour tests
description: Use a local bare git repository as a fake remote to test update detection across commit advance, force-push, branch deletion and offline. Test ignore semantics, auto-update on clean versus locally modified skills, failure recovery, and preset apply and unapply ratios including member deletion.
acceptance: Update checks return the expected state for advanced commit, unchanged commit, force-push, deleted branch and offline.
Auto-update skips a locally modified skill and updates it only on explicit override with a backup.
A preset apply then unapply restores the exact deployment tree hash, and previously enabled members stay enabled.
Applied ratios match the DB after member deletion and after a member is re-added.
Ignoring a sha hides the badge until a newer sha is discovered, across a simulated restart.
notes: Fake remote setup and teardown live in a shared test helper; no network access.
